# 8.3 · JSON Wrangler

`Level 8: Ship It` · `+25 XP` · `drill 3 of 3`

## The job
Get structured data out of what a model actually wrote. `strip_fences` returns the inside
of the first triple-backtick code block, or the text unchanged. `find_json_span` returns the
first balanced JSON object or array, ignoring brackets inside strings. `remove_trailing_commas`
deletes commas that sit right before a closing bracket, but never inside strings.
`extract_json` chains them and parses, raising ValueError when there is nothing usable.
`validate(obj, schema)` checks required and optional (`name?`) fields and their types.

## Why it matters
"Please reply in JSON" works most of the time, and production code has to survive the rest:
a chatty preamble, a fenced block, a trailing comma, a brace inside a quoted string.
Validating the parsed result against a schema is the second half: valid JSON with the
wrong shape breaks your app just as hard as invalid JSON.

## Run it

```bash
python fullsend.py check 8.3     # judge your drill.py
python fullsend.py hint 8.3      # one hint at a time
```

<details><summary>All hints (try the drill first)</summary>

1. Scan character by character with three pieces of state: a stack of expected closing brackets, whether you are inside a string, and whether the previous character was a backslash.
2. A quote character only toggles the in-string state when it is not escaped.
3. Mismatched or missing closing brackets mean there is no valid span: raise ValueError.
4. For trailing commas: outside strings, when you see a comma, peek past any whitespace; if the next character closes an object or array, drop the comma.
5. In `validate`, keys ending in a question mark are optional. Booleans are not integers here either.

</details>
